title: The finite coefficient core of a presentation is a Noetherian base model
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with a specified finite presentation
$$\alpha:A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}B$$
of $A$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], where $n,m\ge0$. Let $A_0\subseteq A$ be the smallest subring containing the image of $\mathbf Z$ and all coefficients of all the $F_j$. Then $A_0$ is a finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Every $F_j$ is obtained by applying $A_0\hookrightarrow A$ to the coefficients of a unique polynomial $F_j^0\in A_0[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. Put $B_0=A_0[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(F_1^0,\ldots,F_m^0)$; this is a finitely presented $A_0$-algebra. Write $\bar t_i=\alpha([t_i])$. The map
$$B_0\otimes_{A_0}A\longrightarrow B,\qquad[P]\otimes a\longmapsto aP(\bar t_1,\ldots,\bar t_n)$$
is an $A$-algebra isomorphism, where tensor products carry multiplication $(b\otimes a)(c\otimes e)=bc\otimes ae$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Its inverse sends the image of $a\in A$ to $1\otimes a$ and $\bar t_i$ to $[t_i]\otimes1$. More generally, for every commutative $A_0$-algebra $C$, the canonical $C$-algebra map
$$B_0\otimes_{A_0}C\xrightarrow{\sim}C[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(F_1^{0,C},\ldots,F_m^{0,C}),\qquad[P]\otimes c\longmapsto c[P]$$
is an isomorphism, where $F_j^{0,C}$ is obtained from $F_j^0$ by applying $A_0\to C$ to coefficients. No injectivity or flatness of $A_0\to C$ is assumed.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line per clause: for the Mathlib presentation P of B over A with val i = alpha([t_i]) and relations F_j (Algebra.Presentation.naive, Basic.lean:511, transported along alpha by Algebra.Presentation.ofAlgEquiv, Basic.lean:162), take A_0=P.Core (core, line 52; Core, line 65). Coefficient containment is coeffs_subset_core (55), and finite type is Algebra.Presentation.instFiniteTypeIntCoreOfFinite (79). Apply Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing in Mathlib/RingTheory/FiniteType.lean:187 with R=Z; the Noetherian instance is PrincipalIdealRing.isNoetherianRing in Mathlib/RingTheory/PrincipalIdealDomain.lean:115. The descended relations are relationOfHasCoeffs (122) with map_relationOfHasCoeffs (125); uniqueness follows coefficientwise from injectivity of the subring inclusion. ModelOfHasCoeffs (142) is the stated quotient; Algebra.Presentation.instFinitePresentationModelOfHasCoeffsOfFinite (145) is its finite-presentation instance. tensorModelOfHasCoeffsEquiv (207), tensorModelOfHasCoeffsEquiv_tmul (212), and tensorModelOfHasCoeffsEquiv_symm_tmul (217) give the isomorphism and both formulas, after tensor-factor symmetry Algebra.TensorProduct.comm in Mathlib/RingTheory/TensorProduct/Maps.lean:380 (formula comm_tmul at 388). For the final C clause, use Algebra.Presentation.baseChange in Mathlib/RingTheory/Extension/Presentation/Basic.lean:294, whose relation is explicitly the coefficient map at 296, followed by Algebra.Presentation.quotientEquiv at Basic.lean:84 and tensor symmetry. This applies to the presentation of B_0 itself, namely Algebra.Presentation.naive (Basic.lean:511, relations F_j^0 by naive_relation_apply at 522), so the chosen relations stay exactly F_j^0, without any injectivity assumption on A_0 to C. All other lines are in Core.lean unless another file is specified.
